how_to_use: The command list is ranked by OPPORTUNITY = genuine signal magnitude × edge remaining × leading-vs-lagging gap — NOT by how many desks agree (agreement is a lagging, consensus condition). 'emerging' = a leading desk firing ahead of a quiet crowd with most of the move still ahead (where the edge is); 'exhausted' = already run, fade-risk. catalysts = fresh dated special-situation events. Every dossier names what would change its read and its edge_remaining; track both.
disclaimer: Context only — five research desks fused into one read per name, never a trade instruction and never a position size.

gate.method: rigorous daily-HAC signed IC (Newey-West lag=horizon), never pooled Spearman

signal_governor.note: No signal has cleared the de-escalation gate yet — all trust 1.0 (shadow/measuring).
signal_governor.disclaimer: De-escalation-only signal governor. A signal is demoted ONLY once its matured, overlap-robust track record proves it mis-firing; trust never exceeds 1.0 and never sizes a position. Absent ⇒ hub is ungoverned.

track_record.note: Measuring — accruing forward observations; the hub's edge is not yet statistically proven. Early numbers are provisional, context-only.

accrual_gaps.note: Expected dates are pandas business days — NYSE market holidays inside the window are counted as gaps, so this over-reports rather than under-reports.

track_record.disclaimer: An accountable scorecard of the hub's own claims — opportunity rank and lifecycle stage graded against realized SPY-relative forward returns. Until a signal matures and clears a Newey-West significance bar it is 'measuring', never trusted. Nothing here sizes a position.

auto_findings.text: 10d: departed names (+7.2% avg) OUTPERFORM on-desk names (+5.1%) — the desk may be exiting winners too early.
10d: 'exhausted' (-0.9%) outperforms 'emerging' (-2.2%) — possible residual inversion in the lifecycle staging.
30d: score VELOCITY IC (+0.002) exceeds LEVEL IC (-0.021) — the change in the desk's score ranks winners better than its level.
30d: departed names (+2.9% avg) OUTPERFORM on-desk names (+0.9%) — the desk may be exiting winners too early.
60d level IC is significantly NEGATIVE (-0.047, n=69161) — the desk's ranking is anti-predictive here; consider inverting or gating the score.
60d: score VELOCITY IC (+0.007) exceeds LEVEL IC (-0.047) — the change in the desk's score ranks winners better than its level.
60d: departed names (-5.5% avg) underperform on-desk names (-4.1%) — DROPS ARE CORRECT; the desk sheds names before they lag.

notes.author: wave2
notes.note: 2026-07-04 inversion finding: the OLD hub engine was anti-predictive — pooled opportunity IC ~-0.09 @5d, and 'exhausted' names (+1.84% avg fwd) BEAT 'emerging' (-0.77%). The hub-v3-trajectory overhaul is the fix under test; this grader's engine_version A/B is the experiment that proves whether it worked.

notes.author: wave2
notes.note: PRICE LESSON: grade off data/yahoo/<T>.parquet adjusted closes ONLY. The S&P-1500 breadth close cache (data/breadth/_closes_cache.parquet) is SPLIT-CORRUPTED — using it silently poisons every RS / forward-return number. A name missing from yahoo is a coverage skip here, never a wrong return.

notes.author: wave2
notes.note: NOTE on the engine_version A/B: the historical hub ledger carries NO engine_version stamp (all ~63k rows pre-date the stamp), so the pre/post-overhaul split only begins accruing from 2026-07-04 forward. Until enough hub-v3-trajectory rows mature, the A/B reads one-sided; that is expected, not a bug.

desk_grader.disclaimer: An accountable scorecard of this desk's own surfaced names — its ranking score (level AND velocity) graded against realized SPY-relative forward returns at 5/10/20/30/60/90 trading days, split on-desk vs after-leaving. A signal is 'proven' only past n>=40 with a significant Newey-West t of the right sign; a significant negative IC is an 'alarm'. Context-only — nothing here sizes a position.
